title: IMemoryCache and IDistributedCache (Redis-backed)
hook: Caching stores expensive results so the next request is fast. IMemoryCache lives inside one server process; IDistributedCache (often Redis) shares cache entries across every instance of your API.

blocks.text: ASP.NET Core offers two primary cache abstractions. IMemoryCache stores objects in the current process heap — fastest lookup, but invisible to other pods or servers. IDistributedCache serializes values to a shared store (Redis, SQL Server, NCache) so horizontal scale-out sees the same keys. Both use string keys, optional absolute and sliding expiration, and callbacks on eviction. Neither is a database — treat cache as an acceleration layer with explicit invalidation and TTL (time-to-live) policies.

entries.plainDefinition: Process-local cache backed by concurrent storage with expiration and optional size limits.
Cross-process cache storing byte arrays; Redis is the common production backend.
Duration a cache entry remains valid before automatic expiration.
Many concurrent requests miss cache simultaneously and all hit the database.
entries.example: Hot key expires → hundreds of parallel DB queries

blocks.text: After onboarding a large customer, read-heavy endpoints suddenly serve ten times more distinct keys — memory pressure rises and Redis round-trips dominate latency. Choosing the wrong cache layer causes stale data across instances (memory-only cache on a farm) or thundering herd on hot keys (no stampede protection). Senior interviews expect you to explain GetOrCreateAsync locking, Redis single-flight patterns, and when cache-aside beats read-through.

blocks.title: Cache is not source of truth
blocks.body: Always define TTL, invalidation on writes, and graceful degradation when Redis is down — serve from the database with higher latency rather than failing the request unless the data is strictly optional.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Build cache key
items.body: Include tenant id, entity id, and schema version — avoid collisions across customers.

items.title: Try cache get
items.body: IMemoryCache.TryGetValue or IDistributedCache.GetAsync returns hit or miss.

items.title: On miss, load source
items.body: Query database or call downstream API once (with stampede protection).

items.title: Set with expiration
items.body: Write entry with absolute and sliding expiration; serialize for distributed cache.

items.title: Return value
items.body: Subsequent requests hit cache until TTL or explicit remove.

snippet.label: Register memory and Redis distributed cache
snippet.explanation: SizeLimit prevents unbounded heap growth. InstanceName prefixes all Redis keys for this service — critical when sharing a Redis cluster.

snippet.label: GetOrCreateAsync with stampede protection (memory cache)
snippet.explanation: GetOrCreateAsync holds a per-key lock so only one factory runs on miss — others await the same Task. Always set Size when SizeLimit is configured.

snippet.label: Distributed cache with JSON serialization
snippet.explanation: IDistributedCache stores bytes — you own serialization. Version keys when DTO shape changes to avoid deserializing stale payloads. This naive path has no stampede protection — see Redis lock snippet next.

snippet.label: Redis distributed lock — cache stampede protection on hot key
snippet.explanation: IDistributedCache has no GetOrCreateAsync lock — Redis SET NX single-flight prevents 500 parallel DB hits when a hot tenant dashboard key expires after onboarding. Add TTL jitter so keys do not all expire together.

snippet.label: Failure-mode — Redis down, fall back to database
snippet.explanation: Production APIs degrade gracefully when Redis fails open to DB. Alert on RedisConnectionException rate — not every miss should become a DB hit forever.

blocks.title: Process cache vs Redis in Node
Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Caching Entity Framework tracked entities (state leaks across requests). Same cache key for all tenants (cross-tenant data leak). No TTL on IMemoryCache (memory leak after onboarding spike). Assuming IDistributedCache has GetOrCreate — implement single-flight yourself for Redis.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: emit OpenTelemetry counters cache.hit and cache.miss per endpoint. Redis INFO keyspace_hits/misses and evicted_keys explain memory pressure after bulk onboarding. Correlate DB query spikes with Redis key TTL expiry — classic stampede signature. Hybrid L1 (30s memory) + L2 Redis reduces cross-AZ RTT on hot dashboard keys.

blocks.title: When to use which cache layer
rows: Reference data, per-pod hot keys, L1 in front of Redis
Must be instantly consistent across all instances
Farm-wide catalog, rate limit counters, session-like data
Large payloads (>1 MB) — cache a pointer to blob storage

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying IMemoryCache works across Kubernetes pods. Ignoring cache stampede when a hot key expires. Omitting tenant id from keys. Claiming Redis is always faster — network RTT on tiny objects can lose to an indexed database query.

interviewTakeaways: IMemoryCache is process-local; IDistributedCache (Redis) shares entries across scaled API instances.
When not to use: strongly consistent reads, huge payloads, or when invalidation is harder than the query.
Production tip: version keys, set SizeLimit, GetOrCreateAsync or Redis lock against stampede, degrade when Redis is down.

60s: Cache-aside — try get, on miss load DB once with lock, set TTL, return. Memory for L1 speed, Redis for farm consistency. Invalidate on writes. Stampede = parallel misses at expiry — single-flight fixes it.
Follow-up: how would you invalidate catalog cache for one tenant after bulk import without flushing all Redis?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'we use IMemoryCache with five replicas' gets you rejected — each pod has its own heap until TTL diverges.
Caching EF tracked entities — stale navigation properties and cross-request state bugs.
Strong answer: 'L1 memory 30s + L2 Redis 5min, tenant-scoped keys, RemoveAsync on write, distributed lock on hot key rebuild after onboarding.'
introducedIn: IMemoryCache since ASP.NET Core 1.0; StackExchange.Redis provider is the production default
